clue.text: But for a bishop, the church's forgiveness is the answer

indicators.note: but for means except for, so the letters for a bishop are left out of the longer word

parts.note: absolution is the forgiveness of sins pronounced by a priest
A as written plus B, the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman remarks that, bishops apart, the church's pardon solves everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But for' here means 'without': AB (a bishop) is removed from ABSOLUTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A solution is a synonym for the reply that resolves a problem or puzzle.

clue.text: Secretly getting uplift from bras or bustiers

indicators.note: uplift says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lingerie advertising: a lift you get from your underwear without anyone knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' marks the letters ASORBUS concealed in 'bras or bustiers'; in a down clue 'uplift' turns them upwards, reading SUBROSA.
explanation.definitionFit: Sub rosa, Latin for 'under the rose', is an idiom meaning in secret, so it fits 'secretly'.

clue.text: Thus was the Olympic cauldron London's opening ceremony's centrepiece

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from London's
only the centre piece of the synonym is kept, so its outside letters are dropped

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: Recalls the 2012 London Olympics, whose opening ceremony built up to the lighting of the flame.
explanation.walkthrough: L (London's opening) plus IT, the centre of RITE (ceremony). The definition is a whole phrase: the cauldron was set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympic cauldron is set alight at the opening ceremony, so it was ignited, the past participle that fits.

clue.text: You may well tear a strip off this delinquent till looter

definitions.text: You may well tear a strip off this

indicators.note: a delinquent behaves badly, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper might well give a till thief a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear a strip off' is British slang for scolding someone; here it is taken literally, tearing off a sheet. The letters of TILL LOOTER are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavatory paper comes on a perforated cylinder from which sheets are literally torn off.

clue.text: Group, primarily of countries talking economic turkey?

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so the opening letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: A bloc of nations meeting to talk frankly about money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking turkey' is an idiom for speaking frankly; the question mark covers the joke that one country could be Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of eight, as of musicians or singers, is a particular kind of group.

clue.text: Flying Gulf Air, one goes into Economy?

definitions.note: economy used as a modifier, as in economy class, describes something thrifty: an adjectival sense

indicators.note: flying suggests letters tossed about, so they are rearranged
goes says the letter for one leaves the word Air

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A passenger on Gulf Air settles into the cheap seats.
explanation.walkthrough: AIR loses I (one) to give AR, which is shuffled with GULF ('Flying'). The question mark flags the definition as an example of the cheap-seats sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Economy as an attribute means sparing in spending, which is what thrifty means.

clue.text: Thatcher may have applied this doctrine after polling

indicators.note: to poll is to cut off the head, so the first letter is lost

parts.note: a creed is a doctrine or set of beliefs

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher put her political doctrine into practice after winning an election.
explanation.walkthrough: A thatcher is a roofer; 'Thatcher' and 'polling' point to the prime minister and elections. 'Polling' in its old sense, cutting off the head, removes C from CREED.
explanation.definitionFit: Dried stalks of a marsh plant are a traditional roofing material laid by a thatcher.

clue.text: Bent witness present

parts.note: a bent is a natural talent or gift
a voucher is one who vouches for something, a witness

explanation.surface: A corrupt witness turns up at a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like 'corrupt' and 'present' like 'attend', but 'Bent' is a talent and 'present' is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A token exchangeable for goods is a common birthday or Christmas gift.

clue.text: Leery ad is wrong on so many levels!

indicators.note: wrong suggests letters set out incorrectly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A complaint that a suggestive advert is offensive in every possible way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is wrong on so many levels' is a stock phrase of disapproval; split, 'wrong' rearranges LEERY AD and 'on so many levels' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something arranged in tiers or strata has many levels.

clue.text: Cueing arm out of position as beginner goes for plant

indicators.note: letters out of position are rearranged
the beginner of the word Cueing is its first letter, and it goes away

explanation.surface: Snooker advice: a badly placed cueing arm, as when a novice plays.
explanation.walkthrough: Cueing loses its first letter C, and UEING plus ARM is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A pelargonium with bright red flowers is a familiar garden and window-box plant.

clue.text: Pop back briefly, then off out to lunch

indicators.note: back says the word for an attempt is read in reverse

parts.note: to have a pop at something is to have a go, a stab

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A worker nips back to the office for a moment, then heads out for a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pop back briefly' reads as a quick return, but 'Pop' is STAB, turned round by 'back', and 'briefly' is fodder: BRIEFLY THEN rearranged ('off') gives INTHEBELFRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal idioms for being crazy or eccentric; out to lunch means not all there.

clue.text: Carthorse: term in football, used harshly of many players

indicators.note: treating something harshly knocks it about, so the letters are rearranged
term means end, so the last letter of football is taken

explanation.surface: A clumsy footballer is abused as a carthorse by the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carthorse' is football slang for a lumbering player, and 'players' suggests a team, but they are musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written for a symphony band involves many musicians playing together.

clue.text: Spam served on tips of asparagus which one's teeth go around

definitions.note: a noun phrase in sense: one whose teeth go around

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece is served on top of the second

parts.note: spam is unwanted mail sent in bulk, like junk circulars

indicators.note: tips are the first letters of asparagus and which

explanation.surface: Tinned luncheon meat served on asparagus tips.
explanation.walkthrough: Spam is junk mail, not tinned meat. CIRCULARS sits on A and W, the tips of 'asparagus' and 'which'. The definition is loose: a thing whose teeth go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A powered blade with a toothed rim spins as it cuts wood, its teeth rotating.

clue.text: History repeating itself

definitions.meaning: something that is history is finished and done with
to do something again is to do it a second time

explanation.definitionFit: Finished, as in 'it's all done', and once more, as in 'start again'.

clue.text: Accounts for children vandalising safety rail

indicators.note: vandalising wrecks something, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Children are held responsible for damaging a safety barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accounts for' reads as 'explains', but it is a noun phrase: stories told to children.
explanation.definitionFit: Nursery stories of magical creatures and enchantments are narratives told to the young.

clue.text: Excellent way to join Resistance operation?

definitions.text: Excellent way to join Resistance operation?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI in crosswords
Rd is the abbreviation for road, a way
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Parachuting in was a great way for wartime agents to reach the French Resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: AI, RD, R and OP join in order; the whole clue also defines, since agents and supplies were parachuted to the wartime Resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Dropping people or supplies by parachute from aircraft was how agents reached occupied France.

clue.text: One might inadvertently witness porcelain having lid stolen and decline to bid on it

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: in an auction or at bridge you pass when you do not bid

indicators.note: the lid is the top, so the first letter is taken away

parts.note: Derby is a fine English porcelain, as in Royal Crown Derby

explanation.surface: At an auction, chipped porcelain missing its lid gets no bids.
explanation.walkthrough: Derby porcelain is made in the English city of Derby. Without its 'lid', D, it gives ERBY, with PASS above it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone walking past by chance may happen to see an incident, becoming an unintended witness.

clue.text: Mixture of Chromium, Iodine and Uranium is likely to explode

indicators.note: a mixture blends ingredients together, so the letters are stirred up

parts.note: Cr and I are the chemical symbols for chromium and iodine
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A chemistry warning that a blend of chromium, iodine and uranium is unstable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture' and 'explode' suggest chemistry, but the definition means quick-tempered.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective for a person easily roused to anger, someone apt to blow up.

clue.text: Place in Man U goal's settled on day, at first

indicators.note: one piece placed on another comes after it here
at first points to the opening letter of the word day
settled means sorted out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Manchester United goal decides the match on the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man U' looks like Manchester United but 'Man' is the Isle of Man and U is anagram fodder. D (first of day) then UGOALS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital town of the Isle of Man is the island's chief settlement.

clue.text: Wayne's world?

parts.note: the film star John Wayne was nicknamed the Duke, so his realm would be a noble's territory; Wayne's World is also a comedy film

explanation.definitionFit: A duke's realm or rank, and John Wayne was known as the Duke.

clue.text: Order silence as alarm goes off outside

indicators.note: outside says the rearranged letters go around the call for quiet
something going off is disrupted, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone tells everyone to be quiet when an alarm sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: ALARM rearranged gives MARAL, which goes 'outside' SH. 'Order' is a verb: to arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange troops or facts in proper ranks is to put them in order.

clue.text: Time to recall Mary's boy getting one of the worst haircuts in years?

indicators.note: getting joins the boy to what follows

parts.note: a lad is a boy

indicators.note: in places the haircut between the two year letters

parts.note: Y is short for year, so years gives two of them
a DA, short for duck's arse, is a slicked-back ducktail haircut, often mocked

explanation.surface: Mary's son has had one of the most awful haircuts seen for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: DA ('duck's arse') is a 1950s greased ducktail hairstyle. It goes 'in' YY (years). Lady Day, 25 March, was traditionally one of England's quarter days.
explanation.definitionFit: The Feast of the Annunciation commemorates the Virgin Mary, Our Lady, so it is a date for remembering her.

clue.text: Pull out backhand slice to gain Asian title

indicators.note: pull out means extract, so letters are taken from inside the word
a slice is a piece cut from within the word backhand

explanation.surface: A tennis player tries a backhand slice to win a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backhand slice' is a tennis shot, but 'slice' asks for a piece of 'backhand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruler or noble in Central Asia bears this honorific, as in Genghis.

clue.text: Relearnt with teacher in rush

indicators.note: in says one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a rush is a reed, the marsh plant
a schoolmaster is a teacher

explanation.surface: Someone relearnt something by hurrying through it with a tutor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rush' is the plant, not haste.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something again is to learn it once more.

clue.text: Article left on seat for collection

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
bum is British slang for the seat one sits on

explanation.surface: An item left on a chair is collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' is British slang for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of photographs or stamps, or a set of recorded tracks, is a collection.

clue.text: Two ducks in a quack? Way out!

indicators.note: in places the noughts inside the doctor's title

parts.note: a quack is slang for a doctor, abbreviated Dr
a duck is a nought in cricket, so two of them are a pair of Os

explanation.surface: A pair of ducks in a farmyard, quacking, told to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck is a score of nought in cricket; 'quack' is a doctor, not a duck's call.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit is through a hinged panel in a doorway, a way out of a room.

clue.text: Search among adult bodies after wreckage at sea

indicators.note: among places the word for search within the rearranged letters
after wreckage the words are left in pieces, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Rescuers look for the bodies of victims after a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: COMB goes among the letters of ADULT BODIES, rearranged. 'at sea' is not literal: it means confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea is an idiom for being bewildered or confused.

clue.text: Sporting side forgetting last tips for the cup?

definitions.note: tips are the young leaves picked for brewing, a plural sense of the drink's leaf

indicators.note: the final letter is forgotten, so it is dropped

parts.note: a team is a side in sport

explanation.surface: A sports team, forgetting their final opponents, receives tips for the cup competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cup' suggests a sporting trophy; it is a teacup. Tips are the leaf buds used for the drink, as in the British brand PG Tips.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf buds of the plant are brewed in a cup to make the drink.

clue.text: Good heavens, do I have to spell it out?

definitions.text: do I have to spell it out?
definitions.meaning: spelling out one's own term, the speaker's own vocabulary item

explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of surprise, and literally the term I am using, which someone may need spelt out.

clue.text: Second me with Syria in turmoil?

definitions.text: Second me with Syria in turmoil?

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A diplomat volunteers to be posted to Syria during its unrest.
explanation.walkthrough: S, ME and SYRIA are rearranged. 'Second' reads as a time unit but also as 'post on assignment', and the whole clue defines.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission, such as a diplomat seconded to a troubled country.
